section: Earth observation - IRS series, Cartosat, Resourcesat, Oceansat, RISAT, EOS series and applications
subsections: INSAT system - services, bands, FIRST communication satellite

accepted.s: The INSAT system was commissioned in which year?
accepted.x: The INSAT system was commissioned in 1983.
accepted.tq: Use the direct year-recall approach and distinguish the commissioning year from satellite-launch years.
accepted.sec: INSAT system - services, bands, FIRST communication satellite  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: INSAT-1B, associated with the commissioning of the INSAT system, was launched using which of the following?
accepted.x: INSAT-1B was launched on the US Space Shuttle Challenger.
accepted.tq: Test the launch vehicle and platform rather than the satellite series alone.
accepted.sec: INSAT system - services, bands, FIRST communication satellite  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The INSAT system is regarded as one of the largest domestic geostationary communication systems in which region?
accepted.x: INSAT is one of the largest domestic GEO communication systems in the Asia-Pacific region.
accepted.tq: Apply the location-comparison clue to identify the correct regional description.
accepted.sec: INSAT system - services, bands, FIRST communication satellite  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which body is responsible for operating the INSAT system through inter-ministerial coordination?
accepted.x: The INSAT system is run by the inter-ministerial INSAT Coordination Committee, or ICC.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional-identity method: distinguish the coordinating body from operating and remote-sensing organisations.
accepted.sec: INSAT system - services, bands, FIRST communication satellite  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The satellites of the INSAT system are controlled from which facility?
o: Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Tirupati district
accepted.x: INSAT satellites are controlled from the Master Control Facility at Hassan in Karnataka.
accepted.tq: Test the specific location of the control facility against nearby space institutions.
accepted.sec: INSAT system - services, bands, FIRST communication satellite  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the services provided through the INSAT system:
1. It supports telecommunication and television services.
2. It provides meteorological services.
3. It supports telemedicine and tele-education.
4. It has no role in search-and-rescue operations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: INSAT supports telecommunication, television, meteorology, telemedicine and tele-education. It also supports COSPAS-SARSAT search-and-rescue operations, so statement 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Find the one reversed service statement and select the corresponding coded combination.
accepted.sec: INSAT system - services, bands, FIRST communication satellite  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: In the INSAT disaster-warning system, which of the following correctly describes the signal arrangement?
o: S-band uplink from Chennai and C-band downlink to inland receivers
C-band uplink from Chennai and S-band downlink to coastal DWS receivers
Ku-band uplink from Chennai and Ka-band downlink to coastal DWS receivers
Ka-band uplink from Hassan and C-band downlink to coastal DWS receivers
accepted.x: The disaster-warning system uses a C-band uplink from Chennai and an S-band downlink to coastal disaster-warning-system receivers.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the two frequency bands by checking the direction and receiving location.
accepted.sec: INSAT system - services, bands, FIRST communication satellite  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following frequency bands are carried by the INSAT system?
o: L, X, V, W and Y bands
C, L, M, N and P bands
C, extended-C, Ku, Ka and S bands
accepted.x: The INSAT system carries C, extended-C, Ku, Ka and S bands.
accepted.tq: Recall the complete named list; do not confuse carried bands with bands used by other systems.
accepted.sec: INSAT system - services, bands, FIRST communication satellite  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes APPLE?
o: It was launched on Challenger in 1983 as a meteorological satellite.
It was launched on Ariane-1 from Kourou in 1981.
It was India's first operational IRS satellite launched by a Soviet Vostok vehicle.
It was launched by GSLV-F04 from Sriharikota in 2007.
accepted.x: APPLE was launched on Ariane-1 from Kourou in 1981 and served as India's first experimental geostationary communication satellite.
accepted.tq: Use the correct launch-place and launch-vehicle pair to reject swapped satellite descriptions.
accepted.sec: INSAT system - services, bands, FIRST communication satellite  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: INSAT-4CR, weighing 2,130 kg, was launched in 2007 by which launch vehicle?
accepted.x: INSAT-4CR weighed 2,130 kg and was launched by GSLV-F04 in 2007. It was the heaviest satellite launched from India in its day.
accepted.tq: Match the precise weight and launch vehicle before considering the year-based distractors.
accepted.sec: INSAT system - services, bands, FIRST communication satellite  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: As stated for the INSAT communication fleet, which of the following is correct?
o: There are 19 operational communication satellites, all controlled by IIRS.
There are 10 operational communication satellites, all transferred to NSIL in 2022.
There are 21 operational communication satellites, of which 10 were transferred to NSIL in 2007.
There are 19 operational communication satellites, of which 10 were transferred to NSIL in 2022.
accepted.x: The fleet comprises 19 operational communication satellites, and 10 were transferred to NSIL in 2022.
accepted.tq: Separate the total fleet size from the subset transferred to another organisation and the transfer year.
accepted.sec: INSAT system - services, bands, FIRST communication satellite  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which INSAT satellite was an exclusive weather satellite launched in 2002?
accepted.x: Kalpana-1 was an exclusive weather satellite launched in 2002.
accepted.tq: Use the specialised-purpose clue to distinguish the meteorological satellite from communication and education satellites.
accepted.sec: INSAT system - services, bands, FIRST communication satellite  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: EDUSAT, launched in 2004, was primarily associated with which INSAT service?
accepted.x: EDUSAT was associated with telemedicine and tele-education services under the INSAT system.
accepted.tq: Identify the satellite from its application-specific name and service association.
accepted.sec: INSAT system - services, bands, FIRST communication satellite  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about EOS-05:
1. It weighs 2,367 kg.
2. It was launched by GSLV-F17.
3. It was launched on 4 September 2026.
4. It performs imaging from geostationary orbit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: EOS-05 weighs 2,367 kg, was launched by GSLV-F17 on 4 September 2026, and performs imaging from geostationary orbit.
accepted.tq: Verify each numerical, date, vehicle and orbital detail before selecting the all-correct combination.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The imaging capability of EOS-05 extends from the visible region to which part of the infrared region?
accepted.x: EOS-05 provides multispectral and hyperspectral imaging from the visible region to long-wave infrared.
accepted.tq: Use the spectrum-range endpoints to identify the correct imaging capability.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following applications is NOT associated with EOS-05?
accepted.x: EOS-05 is intended for applications such as floods, cyclones, forest fires, crops and security. Deep-sea submarine communication is not listed among its applications.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the satellite's Earth-imaging application set.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
With reference to India's geostationary satellite applications, consider the following statements:
1. The earlier geostationary 'eyes' of India were weather satellites of the INSAT-3D series.
2. EOS-05 is intended for land imaging rather than being merely a weather satellite.
3. EOS-03 became India's first operational geostationary land-imaging satellite after a successful launch.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The INSAT-3D series represented India's earlier geostationary weather satellites, while EOS-05 is India's first geosynchronous land-imaging satellite. Statement 3 is false because EOS-03 was lost at launch.
accepted.tq: Reject the false success claim and compare the roles of the INSAT-3D series, EOS-03 and EOS-05.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: EOS-03, referred to in the context of geostationary imaging, was:
o: Launched in 1979 as the first experimental EO satellite
Successfully launched in 2021 and made operational immediately
accepted.x: EOS-03 was described as a geo-imaging satellite in the APPSC 2021 context, but it was lost at launch.
accepted.tq: Use the launch-outcome trap: a mission description does not imply successful orbital deployment.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
 a. IIRS — Dehradun
 b. CSSTEAP — Dehradun
 c. Integrated Mission for Sustainable Development — 1992
 d. EOS-05 — GSLV-F17
accepted.x: IIRS and CSSTEAP are both located in Dehradun; the Integrated Mission for Sustainable Development dates to 1992; and EOS-05 was launched by GSLV-F17. In the coded option, these correspond to the correctly aligned pairs.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure common-location pair and eliminate codes that break the listed associations.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Integrated Mission for Sustainable Development, associated with India's capacity-building and Earth-observation applications, covered how many districts?
accepted.x: The Integrated Mission for Sustainable Development, initiated in 1992, covered 174 districts.
accepted.tq: Separate the district count from satellite weights and other numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: All the launches referred to in the context of India's space programme are stated to take place from SDSC-SHAR, located in:
accepted.x: SDSC-SHAR is located at Sriharikota in Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Identify the launch-site location rather than confusing it with the control or training centres.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the sequence of India's early Earth-observation satellite milestones?
o: IRS-1A operational satellite, followed by Bhaskara I experimental satellite
Bhaskara I experimental satellite, followed by IRS-1A as the first operational IRS satellite
APPLE experimental communication satellite, followed by EOS-03 as the first operational IRS satellite
INSAT-3D weather satellite, followed by Bhaskara I as the first operational IRS satellite
accepted.x: Bhaskara I, launched in 1979, was the first experimental Earth-observation satellite. IRS-1A, launched on 17 March 1988, was the first operational IRS satellite.
accepted.tq: Use the first-experimental versus first-operational distinction to establish the sequence.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: IRS-1A, launched on 17 March 1988, was carried by which launcher?
accepted.x: IRS-1A was launched on 17 March 1988 using a Soviet Vostok launcher and was India's first operational IRS satellite.
accepted.tq: Match the satellite's exact launch date with its foreign launch vehicle.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
